- The purpose and scope of the group;
- Its membership, including a convenor;
- Reporting requirements and timeframe;

### 20.3 Reporting

## 21. RELATIONSHIP WITH YARRA RANGES LIBRARY SERVICES

### 21.1 Role of the Manager

The Manager, Yarra Ranges Library Services, or their nominee, shall be an ex officio member of the Committee and shall provide advice and support to the Committee. The Manager is not a voting member.
### 21.2 Advice and Support

The Manager, or their nominee, shall provide the Committee with:

- Information on library service operations, programs, and strategic direction;
- Advice on the feasibility and resource implications of proposed programs;
- Administrative support as agreed from time to time;
- A written report on library service activities at each ordinary meeting of the Committee.

### 21.3 Access to Facilities

The Committee may use library premises for its meetings and activities, subject to availability and to any conditions imposed by the Manager or the relevant branch librarian. Use of the Community Room (CR) at any branch shall be booked through the usual bookings process.

### 21.4 Relationship with the Library Service

The Committee is an advisory body to Yarra Ranges Library Services. Its role is to provide community input, recommend programs, and support the library service in meeting the needs of the community. The Committee does not have authority to direct library staff or to make decisions on behalf of the library service, except where such authority has been expressly delegated in writing.

### 21.5 Reporting to Council

The Manager shall report annually to Yarra Ranges Council on the work of the Committee, including its membership, activities, and recommendations.

---

## 22. PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF THE COMMITTEE

### 22.1 Purpose

The purpose of the Programming Committee is to advise and assist Yarra Ranges Library Services in the planning, development, and evaluation of library programs and events for the community. The Committee aims to:

- Reflect the diverse needs and interests of the Yarra Ranges community;
- Recommend programs that support literacy, lifelong learning, and community connection;
- Provide a link between the library service and the community it serves;
- Assist in the promotion of library programs and events.

### 22.2 Scope

The Committee's scope covers all public programming delivered by the library service, including but not limited to:

- Children's and family programs;
- Youth programs;
- Adult programs and events;
- Author talks and literary events;
- Digital literacy and technology programs;
- Cultural and community celebrations;
- Outreach programs.

The Committee may also consider matters relating to collections and services where these relate to programming.

### 22.3 Relationship to Other Committees

The Committee shall work cooperatively with other advisory bodies and community groups within Yarra Ranges, where relevant, to avoid duplication and to maximise community benefit.

---

## 23. OPERATING PRINCIPLES

### 23.1 General

The Committee shall operate in accordance with the following principles:

- **Community focus:** The Committee shall keep the needs and interests of the community at the centre of its work.
- **Inclusivity:** Programs and events should be accessible and welcoming to all members of the community.
- **Collaboration:** The Committee shall work with library staff, community groups, and other partners.
- **Accountability:** The Committee shall report on its activities and use resources responsibly.
- **Transparency:** Committee meetings shall be open to the public, except where matters of a confidential nature are discussed.

### 23.2 Decision-Making

Decisions of the Committee shall be made by consensus where possible. Where consensus cannot be reached, decisions shall be made by a majority vote of members present and voting, in accordance with the voting provisions in Section 14 of this Charter.
## 24. MEETING PROCEDURES

### 24.1 Conduct of Meetings

Meetings of the Programming Committee shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of this Charter, the Local Government Act 2020, and any applicable Council policies relating to meetings and public participation.

The Chair shall preside at all meetings of the Committee. In the absence of the Chair, the Deputy Chair shall preside. In the absence of both the Chair and the Deputy Chair, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside for that meeting.

The Chair shall be responsible for:

- Maintaining order and ensuring that meetings are conducted in a fair and efficient manner;
- Ensuring that all members have a reasonable opportunity to speak on matters under discussion;
- Enforcing the time limits set out in the agenda, subject to the discretion of the Committee;
- Determining questions of procedure and relevance;
- Putting motions to the vote and declaring the result;
- Signing the minutes of the previous meeting once confirmed.

### 24.2 Quorum

A quorum shall consist of not less than half of the current appointed members of the Committee, including at least one Councillor. No business shall be transacted at a meeting unless a quorum is present.

If a quorum is not present within fifteen minutes of the advertised commencement time, the meeting shall stand adjourned to a time and place determined by the Chair, and the matter shall be reported to the Committee at its next meeting.

### 24.3 Order of Business

The order of business at each ordinary meeting shall be as follows, unless varied by resolution of the Committee:

1. Acknowledgement of Country;
2. Apologies and leave of absence;
3. Declarations of interest;
4. Confirmation of minutes of previous meeting;
5. Business arising from the minutes;
6. Reports from library staff;
7. Matters for consideration and recommendations;
8. General business;
9. Date of next meeting;
10. Close.

The Chair may vary the order of business with the consent of the meeting.

### 24.4 Motions

A motion is a formal proposal put to the Committee for consideration. The following provisions apply to the moving of motions:

- A motion may be moved by any member, subject to the provisions of this Charter;
- A motion must be seconded before it can be debated or put to a vote. If a motion is not seconded within a reasonable time, it lapses;
- The mover of a motion may speak to the motion at the time of moving it;
- Once a motion has been moved and seconded, it shall be stated by the Chair before debate proceeds;
- A member may speak once to a motion, unless the Committee grants leave to speak again;
- An amendment to a motion may be moved and must be seconded. An amendment shall be debated and voted on before the motion as amended or unamended;
- A motion may be withdrawn by the mover with the consent of the seconder and the Committee;
- A motion that has been passed may be rescinded at a later meeting, provided that notice of intention to rescind has been given in writing to the Secretary at least seven days prior to the meeting, or that the motion is moved by a majority of members present.

### 24.5 Voting

Voting shall be by a show of hands, unless a ballot is requested by any member and supported by a majority of members present.

Each member present at a meeting, including the Chair, shall have one vote. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chair shall have a second or casting vote, which may be exercised to maintain the status quo or to further the objects of the Committee, at the Chair's discretion.
### 25. Reporting and Accountability

25.1 The Committee is a sub-committee of the Yarra Ranges Library Services Board of Management and operates under the authority delegated to it by the Board. The Committee reports to the Board on a regular basis.

25.2 The Committee shall provide a written report on its activities and recommendations to the Board at least once per quarter, or more frequently if required by the Board or the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Library Service.

25.3 The Chair of the Committee, or their nominee, shall attend meetings of the Board when requested to present the Committee's report and to answer questions from Board members.

25.4 The Committee shall forward all formal recommendations and proposals to the CEO for consideration and implementation. The CEO, or their delegate, shall advise the Committee of the outcome of any such recommendation within a reasonable timeframe.

25.5 The Committee does not have authority to make final decisions on matters of Library Service policy, budget, or staffing, except where such authority is specifically delegated by the Board in writing. All such matters shall be referred to the CEO or the Board as appropriate.

25.6 The Committee shall provide a copy of its minutes to the CEO and to the Board Secretariat following each meeting.

### 26. Communication with the Library Service

26.1 The Committee shall maintain open and effective communication with library management and staff. The Library Programs and Partnerships Coordinator, or their nominee, shall attend each Committee meeting as a staff representative to provide reports and to facilitate communication.

26.2 Committee members may, from time to time, be invited to attend staff meetings or community events to discuss the Committee's work, subject to the approval of the Chair and the relevant manager.

26.3 The Committee shall use the official communication channels of the Library Service for its correspondence, including the designated email address (programming.committee@yarraranges.vic.gov.au) and the internal document management system.

26.4 All external communications, including media releases or public statements, shall be made in accordance with the Library Service's Communications Policy and shall be approved by the CEO or their delegate prior to release.

### 27. Subcommittees

27.1 The Committee may, by resolution, establish subcommittees to consider specific matters or to undertake specific tasks. A subcommittee shall be established for a defined purpose and, where practical, for a defined period.

27.2 A subcommittee shall comprise at least two Committee members, one of whom shall be appointed as the subcommittee's convenor. The Committee may also co-opt additional members with relevant expertise, subject to the provisions of Clause 8.

27.3 A subcommittee shall report on its activities to the Committee at each ordinary meeting of the Committee, and shall make recommendations as appropriate.

27.4 A subcommittee shall not make decisions on behalf of the Committee or the Library Service unless expressly authorised to do so by the Committee.

27.5 The Committee shall review the need for each subcommittee at least annually and may dissolve a subcommittee by resolution.

27.6 Any subcommittee established under this Clause shall operate in accordance with the provisions of this Charter, including those relating to conduct, conflicts of interest, and confidentiality, as far as they are applicable.

### 28. Meeting Schedule

28.1 The Committee shall meet on a monthly basis, ordinarily on the second Wednesday of each month, unless otherwise determined by the Committee. Meetings shall be held at a venue determined by the Chair, which may include the Belgrave Library meeting room, the Lilydale Library Community Room, or an alternative location agreed by the Committee.

28.3 Special meetings may be convened by the Chair at any time, or upon the written request of at least three Committee members. Notice of a special meeting shall be provided in accordance with Clause 29.3.

28.4 The schedule of meetings for each calendar year shall be circulated to all Committee members no later than 15 December of the preceding year.

### 29. Notice of Meetings and Agenda

29.1 The Secretary shall prepare and circulate the agenda for each ordinary meeting no fewer than seven clear days prior to the meeting date. The agenda shall be distributed by email to the designated Committee email address and to each Committee member's nominated email address.

29.2 The agenda shall include, where applicable:

(a) confirmation of the minutes of the previous meeting;
(b) business arising from the minutes;
(c) reports from the Chair, the staff representative, and any subcommittees;
(d) items for discussion or decision;
(e) correspondence received and sent; and
(f) general business.

29.3 For special meetings, the notice and agenda shall be circulated no fewer than three clear days prior to the meeting, unless the Chair determines that an urgent matter requires shorter notice. In such cases, the Chair shall advise members of the reason for the urgency.

29.4 Committee members may request that an item be included on the agenda by advising the Secretary in writing no fewer than five clear days prior to the meeting. Items received after this deadline may be included at the discretion of the Chair, or may be deferred to the following meeting.

29.5 The agenda and associated papers shall be made available to Committee members through the internal document management system. Paper copies may be provided to members who request them.

### 30. Chairing of Meetings

30.1 The Chair shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which they are present. In the absence of the Chair, the Deputy Chair shall preside. In the absence of both the Chair and Deputy Chair, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.
### 31. Quorum and Voting

31.1 No business shall be transacted at a meeting of the Committee unless a quorum is present. A quorum shall consist of five members, of whom at least one shall be the Chair or Deputy Chair.

31.2 If a quorum is not present within thirty minutes of the time appointed for the meeting, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the following week at the same time and place, unless the Chair determines otherwise.

31.3 Questions arising at a meeting shall be decided by a show of hands, or by a poll if any member requests it. Each member present shall have one vote.

31.4 Subject to Clause 31.5, a question shall be decided by a majority of votes cast. The member presiding shall have a deliberative vote only, and in the case of an equality of votes, the question shall be deemed to be lost.

31.5 The Chair may, at their discretion, call for a roll-call vote on any motion. The results of a roll-call vote shall be recorded in the minutes, showing the vote of each member as "For", "Against", or "Abstain".

### 32. Minutes of Meetings

32.1 The Secretary shall cause accurate minutes to be kept of the proceedings of each meeting.

32.2 The minutes shall record:
(a) the date, time, and place of the meeting;
(b) the names of members present and apologies received;
(c) all motions moved, the names of the mover and seconder, and the result of any vote; and
(d) any other business considered necessary.

32.3 The minutes of each meeting shall be circulated to all members with the agenda for the next meeting, and shall be confirmed as a true record at that next meeting, subject to any amendments agreed by the members present.

### 33. Conduct of Meetings

33.1 All meetings shall be conducted in accordance with the current edition of the Yarra Ranges Library Services Meeting Procedures, as adopted by the Board from time to time.

33.2 The Chair shall maintain order and ensure that all members have a reasonable opportunity to contribute to discussion.

33.3 Members shall address the Chair when speaking, and shall not interrupt another member who is speaking.

### 34. Resolutions and Decisions

34.1 The Committee may make decisions by resolution passed at a meeting in accordance with this Charter.

34.2 A resolution may also be passed by the circulation of a written resolution to all members, provided that the resolution is signed by a majority of the members entitled to vote. A written resolution shall be recorded in the minutes of the next meeting.

### 35. Subcommittees and Working Groups

35.1 The Committee may, by resolution, establish subcommittees or working groups to consider specific matters and report back to the Committee.

35.2 A subcommittee or working group shall:
(a) have terms of reference approved by the Committee;
(b) report to the Committee at each ordinary meeting; and
(c) be dissolved upon completion of its task or upon a resolution of the Committee.

35.3 A subcommittee or working group may include persons who are not members of the Committee, at the discretion of the Committee.

### 36. Communication and Records

36.1 The Committee shall maintain a register of its members, including their nominated email addresses and any other contact details.

36.2 The Secretary shall maintain a record of all correspondence received and sent by the Committee.

36.3 All Committee records, including agendas, minutes, and reports, shall be retained in accordance with the Yarra Ranges Library Services Records Management Policy.

The Committee operates under the authority of the Yarra Ranges Council and in accordance with the Local Government Act 2020 (Vic). This charter does not replace or supersede any Council policy, by-law, or statutory obligation.

**4. COMMITTEE STRUCTURE**

**4.1 Membership**

The Committee shall comprise no fewer than seven and no more than eleven voting members, appointed by the Library Manager in consultation with the Director of Community Wellbeing. Membership categories are:

| Category | Number | Appointed By |
|---|---|---|
| Library staff (programming, branch, and outreach) | 3–5 | Library Manager |
| Community representatives | 2–3 | Library Manager, from expressions of interest |
| Council officer (non-voting, advisory) | 1 | Director of Community Wellbeing |
| Young adult representative (aged 16–24) | 1 | Library Manager, from expressions of interest |
| Committee Chair | 1 | Elected by Committee members at first meeting of each term |

**4.2 Term of Office**

Members serve a two-year term, renewable once. Terms are staggered to ensure continuity. A member who misses three consecutive meetings without apology may be deemed to have resigned, at the Chair's discretion.

**4.3 Roles and Responsibilities**

The charter states that the legal_name of Yarra Ranges Library Services is Yarra Ranges Library Services. Record status: current.

- **Chair**: Sets the agenda with staff support, chairs meetings, ensures decisions are recorded, and represents the Committee to Council and external stakeholders.
- **Deputy Chair**: Acts in the Chair's absence; supports the Chair in agenda planning.
- **Secretary (staff role)**: Circulates agendas and minutes, maintains the bookings log for program venues, and tracks action items.
- **Treasurer (staff role)**: Monitors the programming budget, reports on expenditure, and flags variances.
- **Community Representatives**: Bring resident perspectives, champion under-served audiences, and assist with community consultation.
- **Young Adult Representative**: Advises on programs for teens and young adults and supports youth engagement activities.

**5. MEETING FREQUENCY AND QUORUM**

The Committee meets monthly, on the fourth Wednesday of each month, from 10:00 am to 12:00 noon. Meetings are held at the Belgrave Library Community Room unless otherwise notified. Special meetings may be called by the Chair with at least seven days' notice.

A quorum shall be a simple majority of current voting members. Decisions are made by consensus where possible; where a vote is required, a simple majority of those present and voting carries the motion. The Chair has a deliberative vote and, in the event of a tie, a casting vote.

**6. DECISION-MAKING AND VOTING**

- All motions must be moved and seconded by voting members.
- Voting is recorded as "For," "Against," or "Abstain" in the minutes.
- Resolutions affecting the annual programming calendar or budget require a two-thirds majority of those present.
- Urgent decisions between meetings may be made by electronic vote, provided all members are consulted and the outcome is reported at the next meeting.

**7. SUB-COMMITTEES AND WORKING GROUPS**

The Committee may establish time-limited working groups for specific program areas (e.g., Summer Reading Club, Seniors Festival, First Nations programming). Each working group must have a named convenor and a clear terms of reference, and must report progress to the Committee at each monthly meeting.

**7. MEETING PROCEDURES**

3. Confirmation of previous minutes

5. Reports from working groups and sub-committees
6. Correspondence

Agendas shall be circulated by the Secretary no fewer than five working days before each meeting. Members are encouraged to submit items for the agenda to the Secretary no fewer than seven working days before the meeting. Items received after the agenda has been circulated may be considered under general business at the Chair's discretion.

Minutes shall record the names of members present, apologies, all motions and their movers and seconders, the outcome of any votes (recorded as "For," "Against," or "Abstain"), and action items with named owners and due dates. Draft minutes shall be circulated within ten working days of the meeting and confirmed at the next meeting.

**8. SUB-COMMITTEES AND WORKING GROUPS (CONTINUED)**

Working groups may be established for a defined term, not exceeding the end of the current programming year, unless renewed by resolution of the Committee. Each working group must have a named convenor and a clear terms of reference, and must report progress to the Committee at each monthly meeting. Working groups may not make public statements or commit the Library to expenditure without prior approval of the Committee.

Members shall declare any conflict of interest in relation to any matter under discussion. A member with a declared conflict shall not participate in the discussion or vote on that matter unless the Committee resolves otherwise. Declarations shall be recorded in the minutes.

**11. ACCOUNTABILITY AND REPORTING**

The Committee reports to the Manager, Yarra Ranges Library Services, and provides a summary of its activities and decisions to the Library's Annual Report. The Chair, or nominee, shall present the Committee's annual report to Council as required. The Committee shall review its own terms of reference and performance annually.

**12. RECORDS AND ACCESS**

Minutes, agendas, and supporting papers are public documents and are available on request, subject to the provisions of the Privacy and Data Protection Act 2014 (Vic). Personal information concerning individual members shall be held in accordance with that Act. The bookings log for program venues is maintained by the Secretary and may be inspected by members on request.

This Charter may be amended by a two-thirds majority of the voting members present at a meeting, provided that notice of the proposed amendment has been given in the agenda. Amendments take effect immediately upon adoption, unless otherwise specified.

### 21.2 Advice and Support

The Manager, or their nominee, shall provide the Committee with:

- Information on library service operations, programs, and strategic direction;
- Advice on the feasibility and resource implications of proposed programs;
- Administrative support as agreed from time to time;
- A written report on library service activities at each ordinary meeting of the Committee.

### 21.3 Access to Facilities

The Committee may use library premises for its meetings and activities, subject to availability and to any conditions imposed by the Manager or the relevant branch librarian. Use of the Community Room (CR) at any branch shall be booked through the usual bookings process.

### 21.4 Relationship with the Library Service

The Committee is an advisory body to Yarra Ranges Library Services. Its role is to provide community input, recommend programs, and support the library service in meeting the needs of the community. The Committee does not have authority to direct library staff or to make decisions on behalf of the library service, except where such authority has been expressly delegated in writing.

### 21.5 Reporting to Council

The Manager shall report annually to Yarra Ranges Council on the work of the Committee, including its membership, activities, and recommendations.

---

## 22. PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF THE COMMITTEE

### 22.1 Purpose

The purpose of the Programming Committee is to advise and assist Yarra Ranges Library Services in the planning, development, and evaluation of library programs and events for the community. The Committee aims to:

- Reflect the diverse needs and interests of the Yarra Ranges community;
- Recommend programs that support literacy, lifelong learning, and community connection;
- Provide a link between the library service and the community it serves;
- Assist in the promotion of library programs and events.

### 22.2 Scope

The Committee's scope covers all public programming delivered by the library service, including but not limited to:

- Children's and family programs;
- Youth programs;
- Adult programs and events;
- Author talks and literary events;
- Digital literacy and technology programs;
- Cultural and community celebrations;
- Outreach programs.

The Committee may also consider matters relating to collections and services where these relate to programming.

### 22.3 Relationship to Other Committees

The Committee shall work cooperatively with other advisory bodies and community groups within Yarra Ranges, where relevant, to avoid duplication and to maximise community benefit.

---

## 23. OPERATING PRINCIPLES

### 23.1 General

The Committee shall operate in accordance with the following principles:

- **Community focus:** The Committee shall keep the needs and interests of the community at the centre of its work.
- **Inclusivity:** Programs and events should be accessible and welcoming to all members of the community.
- **Collaboration:** The Committee shall work with library staff, community groups, and other partners.
- **Accountability:** The Committee shall report on its activities and use resources responsibly.
- **Transparency:** Committee meetings shall be open to the public, except where matters of a confidential nature are discussed.

### 23.2 Decision-Making

Decisions of the Committee shall be made by consensus where possible. Where consensus cannot be reached, decisions shall be made by a majority vote of members present and voting, in accordance with the voting provisions in Section 14 of this Charter.

### 25. Reporting and Accountability

25.1 The Committee is a sub-committee of the Yarra Ranges Library Services Board of Management and operates under the authority delegated to it by the Board. The Committee reports to the Board on a regular basis.

25.2 The Committee shall provide a written report on its activities and recommendations to the Board at least once per quarter, or more frequently if required by the Board or the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Library Service.

25.3 The Chair of the Committee, or their nominee, shall attend meetings of the Board when requested to present the Committee's report and to answer questions from Board members.

25.4 The Committee shall forward all formal recommendations and proposals to the CEO for consideration and implementation. The CEO, or their delegate, shall advise the Committee of the outcome of any such recommendation within a reasonable timeframe.

25.5 The Committee does not have authority to make final decisions on matters of Library Service policy, budget, or staffing, except where such authority is specifically delegated by the Board in writing. All such matters shall be referred to the CEO or the Board as appropriate.

25.6 The Committee shall provide a copy of its minutes to the CEO and to the Board Secretariat following each meeting.

### 26. Communication with the Library Service

26.1 The Committee shall maintain open and effective communication with library management and staff. The Library Programs and Partnerships Coordinator, or their nominee, shall attend each Committee meeting as a staff representative to provide reports and to facilitate communication.

26.2 Committee members may, from time to time, be invited to attend staff meetings or community events to discuss the Committee's work, subject to the approval of the Chair and the relevant manager.

26.3 The Committee shall use the official communication channels of the Library Service for its correspondence, including the designated email address (programming.committee@yarraranges.vic.gov.au) and the internal document management system.

26.4 All external communications, including media releases or public statements, shall be made in accordance with the Library Service's Communications Policy and shall be approved by the CEO or their delegate prior to release.

### 27. Subcommittees

27.1 The Committee may, by resolution, establish subcommittees to consider specific matters or to undertake specific tasks. A subcommittee shall be established for a defined purpose and, where practical, for a defined period.

27.2 A subcommittee shall comprise at least two Committee members, one of whom shall be appointed as the subcommittee's convenor. The Committee may also co-opt additional members with relevant expertise, subject to the provisions of Clause 8.

27.3 A subcommittee shall report on its activities to the Committee at each ordinary meeting of the Committee, and shall make recommendations as appropriate.

27.4 A subcommittee shall not make decisions on behalf of the Committee or the Library Service unless expressly authorised to do so by the Committee.

27.5 The Committee shall review the need for each subcommittee at least annually and may dissolve a subcommittee by resolution.

27.6 Any subcommittee established under this Clause shall operate in accordance with the provisions of this Charter, including those relating to conduct, conflicts of interest, and confidentiality, as far as they are applicable.

### 28. Meeting Schedule

28.1 The Committee shall meet on a monthly basis, ordinarily on the second Wednesday of each month, unless otherwise determined by the Committee. Meetings shall be held at a venue determined by the Chair, which may include the Belgrave Library meeting room, the Lilydale Library Community Room, or an alternative location agreed by the Committee.

28.2 The Committee shall hold no fewer than ten ordinary meetings per calendar year. The December meeting may be combined with the January meeting at the discretion of the Chair, provided that the combined meeting is held no later than the third week of January.

28.3 Special meetings may be convened by the Chair at any time, or upon the written request of at least three Committee members. Notice of a special meeting shall be provided in accordance with Clause 29.3.

28.4 The schedule of meetings for each calendar year shall be circulated to all Committee members no later than 15 December of the preceding year.

### 29. Notice of Meetings and Agenda

29.1 The Secretary shall prepare and circulate the agenda for each ordinary meeting no fewer than seven clear days prior to the meeting date. The agenda shall be distributed by email to the designated Committee email address and to each Committee member's nominated email address.

29.2 The agenda shall include, where applicable:

(a) confirmation of the minutes of the previous meeting;
(b) business arising from the minutes;
(c) reports from the Chair, the staff representative, and any subcommittees;
(d) items for discussion or decision;
(e) correspondence received and sent; and
(f) general business.

29.3 For special meetings, the notice and agenda shall be circulated no fewer than three clear days prior to the meeting, unless the Chair determines that an urgent matter requires shorter notice. In such cases, the Chair shall advise members of the reason for the urgency.

29.4 Committee members may request that an item be included on the agenda by advising the Secretary in writing no fewer than five clear days prior to the meeting. Items received after this deadline may be included at the discretion of the Chair, or may be deferred to the following meeting.

29.5 The agenda and associated papers shall be made available to Committee members through the internal document management system. Paper copies may be provided to members who request them.

### 30. Chairing of Meetings

30.1 The Chair shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which they are present. In the absence of the Chair, the Deputy Chair shall preside. In the absence of both the Chair and Deputy Chair, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

### 31. Quorum and Voting

31.1 No business shall be transacted at a meeting of the Committee unless a quorum is present. A quorum shall consist of five members, of whom at least one shall be the Chair or Deputy Chair.

31.2 If a quorum is not present within thirty minutes of the time appointed for the meeting, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the following week at the same time and place, unless the Chair determines otherwise.

31.3 Questions arising at a meeting shall be decided by a show of hands, or by a poll if any member requests it. Each member present shall have one vote.

31.4 Subject to Clause 31.5, a question shall be decided by a majority of votes cast. The member presiding shall have a deliberative vote only, and in the case of an equality of votes, the question shall be deemed to be lost.

31.5 The Chair may, at their discretion, call for a roll-call vote on any motion. The results of a roll-call vote shall be recorded in the minutes, showing the vote of each member as "For", "Against", or "Abstain".

### 32. Minutes of Meetings

32.1 The Secretary shall cause accurate minutes to be kept of the proceedings of each meeting.

32.2 The minutes shall record:
(a) the date, time, and place of the meeting;
(b) the names of members present and apologies received;
(c) all motions moved, the names of the mover and seconder, and the result of any vote; and
(d) any other business considered necessary.

32.3 The minutes of each meeting shall be circulated to all members with the agenda for the next meeting, and shall be confirmed as a true record at that next meeting, subject to any amendments agreed by the members present.

### 33. Conduct of Meetings

33.1 All meetings shall be conducted in accordance with the current edition of the Yarra Ranges Library Services Meeting Procedures, as adopted by the Board from time to time.

33.2 The Chair shall maintain order and ensure that all members have a reasonable opportunity to contribute to discussion.

33.3 Members shall address the Chair when speaking, and shall not interrupt another member who is speaking.

### 34. Resolutions and Decisions

34.1 The Committee may make decisions by resolution passed at a meeting in accordance with this Charter.

34.2 A resolution may also be passed by the circulation of a written resolution to all members, provided that the resolution is signed by a majority of the members entitled to vote. A written resolution shall be recorded in the minutes of the next meeting.

### 35. Subcommittees and Working Groups

35.1 The Committee may, by resolution, establish subcommittees or working groups to consider specific matters and report back to the Committee.

35.2 A subcommittee or working group shall:
(a) have terms of reference approved by the Committee;
(b) report to the Committee at each ordinary meeting; and
(c) be dissolved upon completion of its task or upon a resolution of the Committee.

35.3 A subcommittee or working group may include persons who are not members of the Committee, at the discretion of the Committee.

### 36. Communication and Records

36.1 The Committee shall maintain a register of its members, including their nominated email addresses and any other contact details.

36.2 The Secretary shall maintain a record of all correspondence received and sent by the Committee.

36.3 All Committee records, including agendas, minutes, and reports, shall be retained in accordance with the Yarra Ranges Library Services Records Management Policy.
